name: High-voltage transformers
summary: High-voltage transformers: microwave oven (MOT), neon sign, ignition and CRT flyback.
uses: Rewinding a MOT into a spot welder or high-current, low-voltage supply
Heavy copper wire and steel cores
Replacement igniters for oil burners and engines
identify: A MOT is a heavy steel-core block (3–6 kg) beside the magnetron, with thick and thin windings; neon sign transformers are tar-filled metal boxes; flybacks are black blocks with a thick red wire in CRT sets. A powered MOT secondary kills.
test: Check winding continuity with the power off. Never power-test a MOT secondary.
